title: Book 5 — Terpsichore, Chapter 114
paragraphs: The men of Amathus then cut off the head of Onesilus, because he had besieged them, and having brought it to Amathus, hung it over the gate of the city. As the head hung there, once it had become hollow, a swarm of bees entered it and filled it with honeycomb. When this had come to pass, the Amathusians consulted an oracle about the head, and they received an answer bidding them take it down and bury it, and sacrifice yearly to Onesilus as a hero; and if they did this, things would go better for them.
